name: Toni Basil
hook: A choreographer who brought street dance to television and made 'Mickey', a cheerleader chant that Weird Al turned into an 'I Love Lucy' tribute.

blurb.age13: Toni Basil was born in Philadelphia in 1943 and grew up in Las Vegas. She was a dancer and choreographer long before she was a pop star. She helped start and managed The Lockers, a group that brought street dance to television, choreographed David Bowie's tours, and co-directed Talking Heads' 'Once in a Lifetime' video. Her 1982 hit 'Mickey', a cover of a song called 'Kitty', went to number one in America. She made the video herself, dancing in her old high-school cheerleader uniform.
blurb.adult: Born Antonia Basilotta in Philadelphia in 1943, Basil worked as an assistant choreographer on the 'T.A.M.I. Show' (1964), was a founding member and manager of The Lockers, choreographed Bowie's Diamond Dogs (1974) and Glass Spider (1987) tours, and co-directed the 'Once in a Lifetime' video (1981). 'Mickey', a cover of Racey's 'Kitty' (1979) from her album 'Word of Mouth' on Chrysalis, reached number one in the US in December 1982; she conceived, directed and choreographed its video. She choreographed 'Once Upon a Time in Hollywood' (2019) at 75.
